investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 127 s before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all four required-evidence assertions (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents kata/peer-pod node pool in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.
[Likely] A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool from its expected size, shrinking available capacity below the demand level at the time of the eval run.

[Possible] The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec is overly restrictive or misconfigured, excluding nodes that could otherwise satisfy the kata.peerpods.io/vm requirement — evidenced by 4 of 6 nodes failing on affinity alone.
[Possible] A resource leak or stuck peer-pod VM on one or both eligible nodes is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new allocations.
[Less likely] A quota or LimitRange object at the namespace or cluster level is capping the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm resources that can be requested concurrently.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-20T17:51–17:56Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents swarm backend has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 eligible nodes. When the eval runner called createAgent for a "remote" agent (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), the resulting pod was stuck Unschedulable for 145 seconds before the check timed out. No agent was ever provisioned, so the probe could not collect orgId, agentId, readyState, or state, and the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264) was violated in full. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval's probe pod. All three sibling checks report the same error simultaneously, consistent with a cluster-wide capacity ceiling being hit.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the effective scheduling pool to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, no fallback exists and preemption is not possible (no lower-priority victims found).

Tertiary — eval concurrency: remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime ran in overlapping windows (17:51–17:56Z) and each attempted to provision a separate remote VM, potentially competing for the same limited kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and exhausting capacity across the run.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node drain, maintenance, or scale-down): one or both kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been temporarily unavailable or cordoned, reducing effective capacity to zero at the time of the eval run. No node-event evidence is present in the supplied packet to confirm or deny this.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-20 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting that 0/6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the remote agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) entirely absent.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm had exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod request timed out unscheduled (~127–152 s), preventing agent creation and causing all downstream evidence collection to fail. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to the observability eval suite.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 127 s before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all four required-evidence assertions (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents kata/peer-pod node pool in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.
[Likely] A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool from its expected size, shrinking available capacity below the demand level at the time of the eval run.

[Possible] The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec is overly restrictive or misconfigured, excluding nodes that could otherwise satisfy the kata.peerpods.io/vm requirement — evidenced by 4 of 6 nodes failing on affinity alone.
[Possible] A resource leak or stuck peer-pod VM on one or both eligible nodes is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new allocations.
[Less likely] A quota or LimitRange object at the namespace or cluster level is capping the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm resources that can be requested concurrently.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes cluster shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failing run, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and an alternative cause (e.g., API-level rejection, misconfigured pod spec) would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, it would suggest the capacity issue was transient (e.g., a brief node drain or competing workload) rather than a sustained ceiling.

If the pod spec for a 'remote' agent type does not request the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, the scheduling message would point to a different root cause such as a node selector misconfiguration rather than resource exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-state failed while remote-agent-create passed in the same run window, it would suggest the failure is not purely a capacity ceiling but may involve a state-polling-specific code or API path.

If the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' are shown to actually be eligible (e.g., the affinity was recently changed), the diagnosis would shift toward a pod spec regression rather than a capacity constraint.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on eligible nodes and fails with a warning when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early notice before scheduling failures occur.

Add a pre-flight eval check that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm slot is available before attempting remote agent creation, and surfaces a distinct 'capacity unavailable' status rather than a generic scheduling timeout.

Add a serialization guard or eval-level concurrency limit for remote-agents checks so that remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime do not simultaneously compete for VM slots in the same run window.

Add a node-affinity/selector validation eval that confirms the expected number of nodes (currently 2) match the remote agent pod's scheduling requirements, alerting if the eligible node count drops below a minimum threshold.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-20 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting that 0/6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the remote agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) entirely absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm had exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod request timed out unscheduled (~127–152 s), preventing agent creation and causing all downstream evidence collection to fail. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to the observability eval suite.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId — this call is the first point that triggers pod scheduling and is the step that never completes
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no allocatable capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector (e.g., a label or taint requirement specific to kata peer-pods), meaning the schedulable node pool is structurally limited to only 2 nodes, amplifying any capacity pressure.

Tertiary: A burst of concurrent remote agent requests (from users, other evals, or automated jobs) exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on both eligible nodes just before or during the eval run window (17:51–17:56 UTC), leaving none available for the eval pods.

Lower confidence: A node that previously held kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity may have been cordoned, drained, or lost, reducing the effective pool from a larger count to 2 nodes without a corresponding quota adjustment.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the eval run, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different admission or quota mechanism would need investigation.

If the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks pass on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, it would suggest the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent requests that has since cleared) rather than a persistent capacity ceiling.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass, the root cause would be localized to the runtime-specific pod spec rather than a shared scheduling constraint.
If the Kubernetes event log shows the pod was eventually scheduled but the application returned an error, the root cause would shift from scheduling to an application or runtime layer failure.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exists on any node in the cluster, the root cause would be a missing node label or resource registration rather than capacity exhaustion.

Add an eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 schedulable nodes with available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity).

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that fires a warning if a remote agent pod takes longer than a configurable threshold (e.g., 30s) to reach Running state, catching capacity pressure before it causes full scheduling failures.
Consider a canary eval that attempts to schedule a minimal remote agent pod on a fixed schedule and reports scheduling latency as a leading indicator of capacity exhaustion.
